issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s status as an Asami under the statutory protection for land let by a disabled landholder does not depend on the same landholder continuing to hold the land until vesting.
material_facts: The original landholder, who was a disabled person, let the land before April 9, 1946.

The original landholder died before the lease expired, and a successor inherited the landholder’s interest; the successor was also a disabled person on April 9, 1946 and continued as landholder until vesting.
The tenants continued to occupy the land and held it on the date immediately preceding vesting.
In consolidation proceedings, the parties disputed whether the tenants remained Asamis or had acquired Sirdar status.
issues.conclusion: The change in the identity of the landholder did not prevent the statutory protection from applying. The tenants remained Asamis and had not become Sirdars.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 21(1)(h) of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, a qualifying occupant is deemed an Asami where the relevant landholder or predecessor in interest was a disabled person on the dates required by the timing of the letting. The term “landholder” incorporates the definition in section 3(26) of that Act and sections 3(1) and 3(11) of the Uttar Pradesh Tenancy Act, 1939, and therefore includes predecessors and successors in interest. Sections 157(1) and 157(2), which permit a disabled person to let a share of a jointly held holding and provide for partition of that share, support the conclusion that continuity of the landholder’s identity is not required. The Court rejected the contrary construction in Smt. Maya v. Raja Dulaji and approved Dwarika Singh v. Deputy Director of Consolidation; the tenants therefore did not acquire Sirdar status under section 240B.

rule.if: tenancy_status_dispute_in_consolidation_proceedings and tenant_occupies_qualifying_capacity_before_vesting and letting_before_cutoff and original_landholder_disabled_at_letting and relevant_landholder_chain_disabled_on_second_material_date

predicates.tenancy_status_dispute_in_consolidation_: The parties disputed the tenants’ tenure status in consolidation proceedings.
predicates.tenant_occupies_qualifying_capacity_befo: The tenants occupied or held the land in a qualifying capacity immediately before vesting.
predicates.letting_before_cutoff: The landholder let the land before the statutory cutoff relevant to determining which material dates apply.
predicates.original_landholder_disabled_at_letting: The landholder who let the land was a disabled person when the letting occurred.
predicates.relevant_landholder_chain_disabled_on_se: The landholder or a predecessor in interest in the chain of title was a disabled person on the second material date applicable to the letting.

issues.definition: When a tenure-status dispute in consolidation proceedings concerns tenants who occupied the land in a qualifying capacity before vesting and the required landholder or predecessor was disabled on the relevant dates, the tenants remain Asamis rather than becoming Sirdars, even if the landholder’s identity changed.
